text:
They started at Fulcrum’s front steps, an instant after the last of the lab staff had gone indoors and locked up. Mara’s mouth felt raw and dry; her throat ached, and her shoulders were rigid and aching too. Her entire body was too hot despite the cold, and she didn’t feel the chill of the night air.
The others were gone. Jonah stood silently beside her, waiting. He was six inches taller than she was. He wasn’t looking at her; his head turned toward the empty drive, and he stared into the darkness beyond the lighted entrance. There was nothing there. She didn’t look. She watched him instead.
“I guess it’s time to go home.” Jonah’s voice was soft, almost inaudible. She had expected more after tonight: analysis or commiseration. Instead he turned sideways with a small sigh and started down the front steps. He swung both arms easily, as though he were on an ordinary walk, though it was the middle of the night and they were both on their way back to hotel rooms in a town she didn’t know.

continuation:
“What’s wrong?” he said. His voice sounded far away, though it was beside her, close to her ear.
“I don’t know,” Mara said. She didn’t know how to answer that question. “Wait for me. I’m sorry I made you wait.”
His steps had stopped on the gravel behind her. He said nothing; he must be waiting. Mara closed her eyes and tried to feel what her body wanted to do. She wished her arms would stop aching, or at least move with something like purpose. She couldn’t feel her own body; everything hurt too much to make any sensation register as useful. She didn’t want him to go away again.
“Come walk with me,” she said, opening her eyes. She turned to face Jonah’s back. She wished he would turn and look at her.
He didn’t look. Instead he came toward her and stopped, facing her. “I’m ready to walk with you. But I’m not going to make you talk right now.”
That was better than walking alone, but it wasn’t what she wanted. She hesitated, then put her hand on Jonah’s arm. He didn’t stop her. His arm felt warm. Mara rested her head against his shoulder for one breath. His skin smelled of sweat and soap. It didn’t smell like sex or cigarettes.
“I’m ready to go now.” Mara turned and started down the road. Her voice made a ringing noise in her skull when she spoke. The sound faded quickly in the open air; Jonah’s feet behind hers made a different noise pattern. She could still hear him. Her eyes adjusted to the light, and she began to see where their footprints had marked the gravel. She walked faster, trying to keep up with herself.
spark:
She went with him, but slowly, letting her legs make her body heavier so she would be one step behind him.
Mara wanted him not to go faster. She wanted to watch how he breathed. Her eyes followed the movement of his hips through the thin denim jeans he wore over black thermal underwear. Mara closed her eyes for one beat and heard the gravel under their feet. His feet made a different sound than hers did; his steps were spaced differently. Mara opened her eyes and stared at the ground. She took deep breaths and slowed, and she let him move away in front of her.
Jonah’s footsteps didn’t falter or slow. She saw his breath as a white cloud, moving with each breath into the cold air.
Her legs went numb below her knees. She realized she hadn’t seen his breath for several seconds, though he must still be breathing. He was gone.
Mara stopped. The sound of Jonah’s footsteps faded away from her left. It made a high, vanishing ring inside her head. “Jonah!” she called, and the sound of her own voice was deafening.
